title: Product Engineering Plain JavaScript Under Pressure Checkpoint

questions.prompt: A is active; B then C are submitted before A settles. What should run next?

options.label: Run C after A settles, and suppress A’s obsolete result.
Run B and C immediately in parallel.
Render A and discard C because A started first.

questions.explanation: The bounded pending slot retains only C. Starting both increases concurrency beyond the contract; keeping A as the visible answer ignores current intent. Completion order cannot determine which input the artist now wants.

questions.prompt: The provider ignores AbortSignal and resolves after dispose. What prevents a stale render?

options.label: AbortController guarantees the provider cannot return.
Removing the spinner cancels remote computation.
A disposed/revision guard before every UI callback.

questions.explanation: Cancellation is a request to cooperating operations. A guard still prevents late local callbacks when cancellation is ignored; changing loading state cannot cancel an operation or prove remote work stopped.

questions.prompt: A fails after B was submitted. What should the coordinator do?

options.label: Keep the active slot occupied permanently.
Suppress A’s obsolete error and continue with B.
Show A’s error as if B failed.

questions.explanation: Errors need the same revision guard as results: A no longer describes current intent. The slot must be released in finally so B can run; otherwise one old failure blocks all future work.

questions.prompt: The active adapter never settles. Which statement is accurate?

options.label: The baseline blocks; a timeout alone does not prove remote work stopped.
The finally block runs after a fixed JavaScript timeout automatically.
Promise.race always cancels the losing operation.

questions.explanation: Finally runs when control leaves the awaited operation, not after an implicit timeout. Promise.race changes which promise you await; it does not stop the remote operation. Define deadline, cancellation, and capacity policy explicitly.

questions.prompt: generate receives a mutable canvas object that is edited again before it reads the data. What is missing?

options.label: A larger result cache keyed only by prompt.
A React component key to freeze the object.
An immutable input snapshot or stable revision reference.

questions.explanation: A revision guard labels an operation but does not freeze its inputs. Snapshot the relevant state or use immutable revision references. A prompt-only cache omits identity, and component keys do not prevent object mutation.

questions.prompt: Can the same replace-newest-pending policy be used for accepted paid exports?

options.label: Yes; a WebSocket connection is a durable queue.
No; accepted exports need durable identity and completion tracking.
Yes; older accepted exports can always be discarded.

questions.explanation: Preview intents are replaceable by the agreed product contract. An accepted export is a durable commitment, so silently coalescing it loses work. A socket is a transport and does not survive failure as a job record.
